answer: Voting power comes from a limited sponsorship market. Each newcomer needs three established sponsors who escrow 40 credits and may back only two entrants per epoch. The grove registry selects sponsors from separate activity clusters; an ocean beacon assigns a public delivery task, and a relic receipt binds its result to one key. If sponsored keys share funding or copied work, every linked escrow loses 70%. A fake-identity farm must therefore recruit scarce independent sponsors, risk their capital, and complete unique work for each key; sponsorships, tasks, and slashes are auditable.
